column7: 2026-11-06: Security (Leo) is reviewing this PR after the old ReDoS advisory against ms: no regular expressions in any new parsing code on this branch. The ISO 8601 duration parse side (next task) must be hand-written. Note: formatISO in src/index.ts uses one regex (.replace(/0+$/, '')) for trimming zeros; it is formatting not parsing, so left as is, but may be worth removing.

2026-11-06: My own choices in formatISO (not user-specified; revisit if asked): zero is PT0S, negatives get a leading '-', input rounds to nearest ms, fractional seconds kept with trailing zeros trimmed, non-finite/non-number throws. Parse side should accept what formatISO emits (round-trip), hand-written, no regex. Committed as 78a8b38; edge-runtime tests not run.

2026-11-06: My own choices in parseCompound (not user-specified): hand-written tokenizer with no regex, because the iso-duration branch's Security review (ReDoS advisory on ms) asked for that and I assumed it applies here too; each part needs a unit (bare '30' is NaN); optional '-' per part; whitespace between parts optional; non-strings/empty/>99 chars return NaN instead of throwing; delegates unit lookup to parse(). Branch feat/compound was cut from feat/iso-duration (contains formatISO commit), so a PR off main would include that commit unless rebased.

2026-11-06: User decision for this PR (overrides my earlier no-regex assumption): parseCompound uses a single anchored regex over the whole string, parse()-style, with input capped at 99 chars, because reviewer Ana prefers regex over hand-rolled loops. The no-regex rule from feat/iso-duration applies to that branch only. Pathological-input test kept.

2026-11-06: parseISO added in src/index.ts (+ src/parse-iso.test.ts), hand-written scanner, no regex. My choices: accepts W/D/H/M/S, optional +/- sign, '.' or ',' fractions; rejects Y/M-in-date (ambiguous), wrong order, empty 'P'/'PT'. Also (mine) removed the one regex in formatISO (trailing-zero trim) so the branch has none. Not committed yet.
